lines.text: This picture looks like a spacecraft falling into a giant crater on Mars. It isn't.
It's NASA's Phoenix lander, hanging under its parachute. The crater is about twenty kilometres behind it.
The photo was taken by this. NASA's Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter, built from NASA's own 3D model.
Its camera, HiRISE, has a telescope mirror half a metre wide. From about three hundred kilometres up, each pixel covers about thirty centimetres of ground.
On May twenty-fifth, two thousand eight, it was seven hundred and sixty kilometres away, moving at three point four kilometres a second. It turned, and caught Phoenix in the air.
It was the first time a spacecraft had photographed another one coming down onto a planet.
The crater is ten kilometres wide. The parachute is a few pixels. The whole story is in that tiny detail.
